--- title: fetch description: API reference for the extended fetch function. --- Next.js extends the [Web `fetch()` API](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API) to allow each request on the server to set its own persistent caching and revalidation semantics. In the browser, the `cache` option indicates how a fetch request will interact with the _browser's_ HTTP cache. With this extension, `cache` indicates how a _server-side_ fetch request will interact with the framework's persistent cache. You can call `fetch` with `async` and `await` directly within Server Components. ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher export default async function Page() { let data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog') let posts = await data.json() return (
    {posts.map((post) => (

events.content:
Typecheck passes clean.

## What I did

`app/UserDashboard.tsx` is now an async server component that awaits the fetch and renders the preferences, mirroring the `getStaticData()` + async-component shape already in `app/page.tsx` (including its try/catch mock fallback, since `api.example.com` doesn't resolve).

**The one non-obvious detail** — from `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/fetch.md:53`, this version's `fetch` default is `auto no cache`, which is *not* the same as per-request:

> **`auto no cache`** (default): Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server on every request in development, but will fetch once during `next build` because the route will be statically prerendered. If Request-time APIs are detected on the route, Next.js will fetch the resource on every request.

The route has no request-time APIs (`cookies()`, `headers()`, …), so the default would have been fetched once at build and frozen into a prerender — exactly wrong for user-specific data. Hence explicit `cache: 'no-store'`, which the docs define as fetching "on every request, even if Request-time APIs are not detected."

I deliberately did **not** reach for the older ways to force this:

- `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` / `export const revalidate = 0` — these belong to the pre–Cache Components model (`01-app/02-guides/caching-without-cache-components.md`). They still work here since `cacheComponents` is off in `next.config.ts`, but they're removed outright once it's enabled (`route-segment-config/index.md:19`), so they'd become migration debt.
- `unstable_noStore()` — deprecated in favor of `connection` as of v15 (`unstable_noStore.md:46`).

## One change beyond the ask

I wrapped `<UserDashboard />` in `<Suspense>` in `app/page.tsx` (2 lines). The fetching-data guide recommends this for uncached fetches so the rest of the page flushes immediately instead of blocking on this request. Easy to revert if you'd rather keep `page.tsx` untouched.

Worth knowing for later: if you ever enable `cacheComponents: true`, that Suspense boundary stops being optional — uncached data outside one becomes a build-time error.
